text:
Igor Shesterkin's season lasted five games. He went down in a fall against Washington on Oct. 9, left after 28 minutes, and the Rangers announced the next day that a right knee injury would keep him out for the rest of the year. He had been excellent until then, saving 4.9 goals more than an average goalie would on the shots he faced (goals saved above expected, or GSAx), allowing 8 on 12.9 expected, with a .927 save percentage and a 3-1-0 record.

That fit the pattern. He was +21.5 last season in 51 games by our measure, Evolving-Hockey had him even higher on their scale, and he has a Vezina from 2021-22. The one blemish this fall was rebounds (15.8% of his saves led to another shot within three seconds, against a league 10.7%), in a tiny sample. The story now is the crease he left. Mike Sullivan has set a Joonas Korpisalo and Dylan Garand split, per Hudson River Blue, and NHL.com's Jon Lane wrote that neither has to be Shesterkin: "They don't have to be and each play their own game." Newsday is asking how the Rangers are surviving. For now, they are.
headline: Rangers learn to live without Igor Shesterkin
